title: Nature of Matter: Elements, Compounds, and Mixtures

learn.hook: Everything around you, from your pencil to the Taj Mahal, is built from just 118 known 'ingredients' called elements!
points: An element is a pure substance made of only one kind of atom. It cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical methods.
118 elements are known today. Examples: hydrogen, oxygen, carbon, iron, copper, gold and sulfur.
Each element has a symbol of one or two letters, the first always a capital: H (hydrogen), O (oxygen), C (carbon), N (nitrogen), Fe (iron), Cu (copper), Na (sodium), Au (gold), Ag (silver).
Most elements are metals. Metals are usually shiny, can be beaten into sheets (malleable) and drawn into wires (ductile), and conduct heat and electricity well.
Non-metals such as sulfur, carbon and oxygen are usually dull and brittle when solid, and are poor conductors. (Graphite, a form of carbon, is an exception: it conducts electricity.)

example.q: Think it through: A shiny piece of material is beaten into a thin sheet and conducts electricity in a circuit. Is it more likely a metal or a non-metal?
steps: Shiny lustre is a property of metals.
Being beaten into sheets (malleability) is a property of metals.
Good electrical conduction is a property of metals.
example.answer: It is most likely a metal.

learn.reallife: Copper is used for electric wires and aluminium for cooking vessels and foil because metals conduct electricity and heat well.

quiz.q: What is an element?
options: A pure substance made of only one kind of atom
A substance made of two elements joined together
quiz.explain: An element has only one kind of atom and cannot be broken down chemically into simpler substances.
steps: An element contains only one kind of atom
It cannot be broken down chemically, so an element is a pure substance made of only one kind of atom
Answer: A pure substance made of only one kind of atom
quiz.mistake: Confuses elements with compounds or mixtures

quiz.q: What is the chemical symbol of iron?
quiz.explain: Iron's symbol Fe comes from its Latin name, ferrum.
steps: Iron's symbol comes from its Latin name, ferrum
So the symbol for iron is Fe
Answer: Fe
quiz.mistake: Assumes every symbol comes from the English name

quiz.q: How many elements are known today?
quiz.explain: Scientists have identified 118 elements so far.
steps: Scientists have identified all the known elements
The total known today is 118
Answer: 118
quiz.mistake: Remembers only the naturally common elements or guesses a round number

quiz.q: Which of these is a non-metal?
quiz.explain: Sulfur is a yellow, brittle non-metal that does not conduct electricity.
steps: Sulfur is yellow and brittle and does not conduct electricity
So sulfur is the non-metal; copper, aluminium and silver are metals
Answer: Sulfur
quiz.mistake: Mixes up metals and non-metals

quiz.q: Which property tells us that copper is used for electric wires?
options: It is a good conductor of electricity
quiz.explain: Copper conducts electricity very well and can be drawn into wires (ductile).
steps: Wires must carry current
Copper is a good conductor of electricity and can be drawn into wires
Answer: It is a good conductor of electricity
quiz.mistake: Does not link the use of a metal with its property

quiz.q: The symbol 'Na' stands for:
quiz.explain: Na comes from natrium, the Latin name for sodium. Nitrogen is N.
steps: Na comes from natrium, the Latin name for sodium
Nitrogen's symbol is N, so Na stands for sodium
Answer: Sodium
quiz.mistake: Guesses from the first letter of the English name

quiz.q: Being able to be drawn into thin wires is called:
quiz.explain: Ductility means a metal can be drawn into wires; malleability means it can be beaten into sheets.
steps: Drawing a metal into wires is ductility
Beating it into sheets is malleability
Answer: Ductility
quiz.mistake: Confuses ductility with malleability

quiz.q: Which statement about elements is correct?
options: They can be broken into simpler substances by heating with acid
They are made of only one kind of atom
quiz.explain: Water is a compound and air is a mixture. Elements contain only one kind of atom.
steps: Water is a compound and air is a mixture
Elements cannot be broken down chemically; they are made of only one kind of atom
Answer: They are made of only one kind of atom
quiz.mistake: Thinks water or air is an element

teach.ask: Gappu pecks at a copper wire: My teacher called copper an 'element'. What does that mean?
teach.praise: An element is a pure substance with just one kind of atom, and it cannot be broken into anything simpler. Copper is one!
teach.nudge: What is an element made of? Can it be broken down into simpler things?

revise.summary: An element is a pure substance of only one kind of atom that cannot be broken down chemically; 118 are known. Each has a one- or two-letter symbol, like Fe for iron and Na for sodium. Most are metals (shiny, malleable, ductile, good conductors); non-metals like sulfur are dull and brittle.
remember: Fe = iron (ferrum), Na = sodium (natrium), Cu = copper, Au = gold, Ag = silver
Malleable: beaten into sheets; ductile: drawn into wires
traps: Water is a compound and air is a mixture, not elements
Graphite is a non-metal that does conduct electricity

learn.hook: Hydrogen is a gas that burns. Oxygen helps things burn. Join them chemically and you get water, which puts out fires! How can that be?
points: A compound is a pure substance formed when two or more elements combine chemically in a fixed proportion.
A compound has properties different from the elements it is made of. Sodium (a very reactive metal) and chlorine (a poisonous gas) form common salt, which we eat.
Every compound has a fixed composition and a formula: water is H₂O (2 hydrogen atoms and 1 oxygen atom), carbon dioxide is CO₂, common salt is NaCl.
A compound can be split into its elements only by chemical methods, not by simple physical methods like filtering or using a magnet.
Energy (like heat or light) is often taken in or given out when a compound is formed.

example.q: Think it through: Iron filings and sulfur powder are mixed. A magnet pulls out the iron. After the mixture is strongly heated in a lab, the new black solid is no longer attracted by the magnet. What happened?
steps: Before heating, iron kept its own property of being attracted to a magnet: it was a mixture.
Heating made iron and sulfur combine chemically.
The new substance, iron sulfide, has new properties, so the magnet cannot pull out the iron.
example.answer: A compound (iron sulfide) was formed, with properties different from iron and sulfur. (This is a lab demonstration only.)

learn.reallife: The sugar in your kheer is a compound of carbon, hydrogen and oxygen, yet it looks and tastes nothing like charcoal or any gas!

games.title: Compound clues
items: A compound has properties different from its elements.
Water puts out fire even though hydrogen burns and oxygen supports burning.
The elements in a compound can be in any proportion.
Elements in a compound combine in a fixed proportion.
Water is made of hydrogen and oxygen.
A magnet can separate iron from iron sulfide.
In a compound the iron is chemically combined, so a magnet cannot pull it out.
A molecule of carbon dioxide has one carbon atom and two oxygen atoms.
That is what the formula CO₂ tells us.

quiz.q: What is a compound?
options: Two or more elements chemically combined in a fixed proportion
Two substances mixed in any amount
A substance with only one kind of atom
quiz.explain: In a compound the elements are chemically joined and always in the same ratio.
steps: In a compound, elements are chemically joined
and always in the same, fixed proportion
Answer: Two or more elements chemically combined in a fixed proportion
quiz.mistake: Confuses compounds with mixtures

quiz.q: Which of these is a compound?
quiz.explain: Water is hydrogen and oxygen chemically combined. Oxygen and gold are elements; air is a mixture.
steps: Water is hydrogen and oxygen chemically combined, so it is a compound
Oxygen and gold are elements; air is a mixture
Answer: Water
quiz.mistake: Thinks air is a compound

quiz.q: How many atoms in total are there in one molecule of water (H₂O)?
steps: H₂ means 2 hydrogen atoms
O means 1 oxygen atom
Answer: 3
quiz.explain: A water molecule has 2 hydrogen atoms and 1 oxygen atom.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the number written as a subscript

quiz.q: Common salt is made of sodium and chlorine. Why is it safe to eat when chlorine is poisonous?
options: A compound has properties different from its elements
quiz.explain: When elements combine to form a compound, the new substance has completely new properties.
steps: When elements combine, the compound has completely new properties
So salt is safe to eat even though chlorine is poisonous
Answer: A compound has properties different from its elements
quiz.mistake: Thinks a compound keeps the properties of its elements

quiz.q: How can a compound be broken down into its elements?
quiz.explain: Elements in a compound are chemically bonded, so physical methods cannot separate them.
steps: Elements in a compound are chemically bonded
Filtering, magnets or sieving cannot separate them; only chemical methods can
Answer: Only by chemical methods
quiz.mistake: Thinks physical methods can split compounds

quiz.q: What does the formula CO₂ tell us?
quiz.explain: C is carbon, O is oxygen, and the small 2 belongs to oxygen.
steps: In CO₂, carbon has no number after it, so there is 1 carbon atom
The small 2 belongs to oxygen, so there are 2 oxygen atoms
Answer: 1 carbon atom and 2 oxygen atoms
quiz.mistake: Reads the subscript as belonging to the wrong element

quiz.q: In a compound, the elements are always present in:
quiz.explain: Every sample of pure water, for example, has hydrogen and oxygen in the same ratio by mass.
steps: Every sample of pure water has hydrogen and oxygen in the same ratio
So elements in a compound are always in a fixed proportion
Answer: A fixed proportion
quiz.mistake: Thinks compounds have variable composition like mixtures

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT a compound?
quiz.explain: Copper is an element. Sugar, carbon dioxide and salt are compounds.
steps: Copper is made of only one kind of atom, so it is an element
Sugar, carbon dioxide and salt are compounds
Answer: Copper
quiz.mistake: Thinks a metal is a compound

teach.ask: Gappu drinks from his bowl: Water is made of two gases? But it is not a gas! How does that work?
teach.praise: Hydrogen and oxygen combine chemically to make the compound water, which has totally new properties. Mind blown!
teach.nudge: What do we call it when elements join chemically? Does the new substance behave like the old ones?

revise.summary: A compound is two or more elements chemically combined in a fixed proportion, with properties different from its elements (sodium + chlorine → edible salt). It has a formula, like H₂O, CO₂ or NaCl, and can be split only by chemical methods. Energy is often taken in or given out when it forms.
focus: Definition of a compound and fixed proportion
Separating compounds only by chemical methods
remember: H₂O: 2 hydrogen + 1 oxygen; CO₂: 1 carbon + 2 oxygen; NaCl: common salt
Heating iron and sulfur forms iron sulfide, which a magnet cannot pull
Compounds have new properties unlike their elements
traps: A magnet or filter cannot split a compound
The small number in a formula belongs to the atom before it
Copper is an element, not a compound

learn.hook: A plate of chivda has poha, peanuts, curry leaves and raisins. You can pick out each one. That is the secret of a mixture!
points: A mixture contains two or more substances mixed physically in any proportion. Each substance keeps its own properties.
Mixtures can be separated by physical methods: handpicking, sieving, using a magnet, decanting, filtration and evaporation.
A homogeneous mixture has the same composition throughout, like salt dissolved in water, air, or brass. A heterogeneous mixture is not uniform, like sand in water or oil on water.
Alloys are mixtures of a metal with other elements: brass is copper and zinc; steel is mainly iron with a little carbon.
Elements and compounds are pure substances: they have a fixed composition. Mixtures are not pure substances.

example.q: Think it through: How would you separate a mixture of salt, sand and iron filings?
steps: Move a magnet (wrapped in paper) over it to pull out the iron filings.
Add water and stir: salt dissolves, sand does not.
Filter: sand stays on the filter paper, salt water passes through.
Evaporate the salt water (with an adult, by heating or in sunlight) to get the salt back.
example.answer: Magnet, then dissolving in water, filtration and evaporation.

learn.reallife: Salt farmers along the coast of Gujarat let seawater evaporate in shallow pans under the sun, leaving salt behind.

quiz.q: Which of these is a mixture?
quiz.explain: Air is a mixture of gases such as nitrogen, oxygen, argon and carbon dioxide.
steps: Air contains nitrogen, oxygen, argon and carbon dioxide mixed together
So air is a mixture; water is a compound, oxygen and iron are elements
Answer: Air
quiz.mistake: Thinks air is a pure substance

quiz.q: Which is a homogeneous mixture?
quiz.explain: Dissolved salt is spread evenly, so every part of the solution is the same.
steps: Dissolved salt is spread evenly through the water
Every part is the same, so salt water is a homogeneous mixture
Answer: Salt dissolved in water
quiz.mistake: Confuses homogeneous with heterogeneous mixtures

quiz.q: Brass is an alloy of:
quiz.explain: Brass is a mixture of copper and zinc used in utensils and taps.
steps: Brass is an alloy used in utensils and taps
It is a mixture of copper and zinc
Answer: Copper and zinc
quiz.mistake: Mixes up brass with steel

quiz.q: How can you get salt back from salt water?
quiz.explain: Dissolved salt passes through a filter, but when the water evaporates the salt is left behind.
steps: Dissolved salt passes through a filter
When the water evaporates, the salt is left behind, so evaporation gets it back
Answer: Evaporation
quiz.mistake: Thinks filtration can remove a dissolved solid

quiz.q: In a mixture, the components:
options: Are always in a fixed ratio
quiz.explain: Each substance in a mixture keeps its properties, which is why physical methods can separate them.
steps: Each substance in a mixture keeps its own properties
That is why physical methods can separate them
Answer: Keep their own properties
quiz.mistake: Applies compound properties to mixtures

quiz.q: Which method separates sand from water?
quiz.explain: Filter paper lets water pass through and holds back the sand.
steps: Filter paper lets water pass through
It holds back the sand, so filtration separates them
Answer: Filtration
quiz.mistake: Picks a method meant for other kinds of mixtures

quiz.q: Which is a pure substance?
quiz.explain: Distilled water is the compound water with nothing else in it. The others are mixtures.
steps: Distilled water is only the compound water, with nothing else
Lemonade, sea water and soil are mixtures
Answer: Distilled water
quiz.mistake: Thinks any clear liquid is pure

quiz.q: Why can a magnet separate iron filings from a mixture of iron and sulfur, but not from iron sulfide?
options: In the mixture iron keeps its magnetic property; in the compound it is chemically combined
The magnet is too weak in both cases
quiz.explain: Mixtures keep the properties of their parts, while compounds have new properties.
steps: In the mixture, iron keeps its magnetic property
In iron sulfide it is chemically combined and the compound has new properties
Answer: In the mixture iron keeps its magnetic property; in the compound it is chemically combined
quiz.mistake: Does not see the difference between a mixture and a compound

teach.ask: Gappu picks peanuts out of his chivda: Is chivda a compound? How is a mixture different from a compound?
teach.praise: Chivda is a mixture: things mixed physically in any amount, keeping their own properties, so I can pick them apart. Crunch!
teach.nudge: Are the things in chivda joined chemically? Can I separate them easily?

revise.summary: A mixture has two or more substances mixed physically in any proportion, each keeping its properties, so physical methods (sieving, magnet, filtration, evaporation) separate it. Homogeneous mixtures are uniform (salt water, air, brass); heterogeneous ones are not. Elements and compounds are pure.
remember: Brass = copper + zinc; steel = mainly iron + a little carbon
Salt + sand + iron: magnet, dissolve, filter, evaporate
Pure substances: elements and compounds; distilled water is pure
traps: Filtration cannot recover dissolved salt — use evaporation
Air is a mixture, not a compound
Components of a mixture keep their properties and need no fixed ratio
